solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Great ruler Henry pursues around border

parts.note: CA = circa, Latin for around, as in dates
a lip is an edge or rim
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A king called Henry chases an enemy across a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like one of England's kings, the obvious great ruler; he is only the physics unit H. 'Around' is not a container signal here but CA, circa.
explanation.definitionFit: A caliph was the supreme ruler of the Islamic world, a great ruler indeed.

clue.text: Officer suggested dismissing one involved in crime

parts.note: CO = commanding officer
implicit means implied, suggested rather than stated
I is the Roman numeral one, removed from IMPLICIT

explanation.surface: An officer hinted at firing a colleague caught up in wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'dismissing' as sacking someone; it just drops one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an accomplice is a partner in the wrongdoing rather than a bystander, which is what the adjective describes.

clue.text: Pale colour of phone casing this person brought round

indicators.note: a casing is an outer shell
the whole is turned about, so it reads upwards in this down clue

parts.note: to phone someone is to call them
'this person' is the writer, I

explanation.surface: Someone describes the pale shade of a phone cover they have brought along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Phone casing' suggests a phone cover, but 'casing' is the verb: CALL wraps round I to make CALIL, then the lot turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a pale purple, named after the blossom.

clue.text: Frank's back from trip, one spent in former East Germany

indicators.note: takes the letter at the back of 'trip'

parts.note: the last letter of trip

parts.words: one spent in former East Germany
parts.note: the Ostmark was East Germany's currency, a coin spent there

explanation.surface: Frank is home from a holiday in the old GDR.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name returning from a trip; it is the noun, the stamp put on a letter. 'One spent' means a unit of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A frank is the mark stamped on mail to show postage is paid, which is what a postmark is.

clue.text: Wrong way to fill pastry, following one's own path

parts.note: milk that is off has gone wrong

indicators.note: filling goes inside a pie

parts.note: a pie is a pastry
ST = street, a way

explanation.surface: A cook goes wrong in the method for filling a pie crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following one's own path' works literally for skiing away from the marked runs and figuratively for doing things unconventionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-piste skiing leaves the prepared runs, so figuratively it means going one's own unconventional way.

clue.text: Riches given to bank worker, one trading in futures

parts.note: a fortune is great wealth
a teller serves customers at a bank counter

explanation.surface: A bank clerk is handed a pile of money by a futures trader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trading in futures' is City jargon for speculative contracts; here it means dealing in what the future holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune-teller makes a living selling predictions, so trades in futures.

clue.text: Invest Asian currency, turning up a bit of capital

parts.note: to put money into something is to invest it
the yen is Japan's currency

explanation.surface: Advice to put some capital into Japanese yen as the currency rises.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'capital' money; it is London, and Putney is a district in south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the capital is London, and this riverside district is one small part of it.

clue.text: Guided munition to fail after vehicle's overturned

indicators.note: what comes after follows behind in sequence

parts.note: trams are vehicles; the 's reads as plural
a show that bombs is a flop

explanation.surface: A missile misfires once the transporter carrying it has tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle's' must be read as 'vehicles', plural, to give TRAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart bomb is steered to its target by laser or GPS guidance.

clue.text: English Master's ditched by doubtful fellow showing spirit

parts.note: E = English
doubting Thomas, the apostle who would not believe until he saw
MA = Master of Arts, the degree; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: An English schoolmaster is dropped by a sceptical colleague with plenty of spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubtful fellow' points to the proverbial doubting Thomas, the disciple who doubted the Resurrection.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic spirit of a group or institution.

clue.text: Exploit really quiet, timid individual

parts.note: to milk a situation is to exploit it
so = really, as in 'so good'
p = piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: Someone takes advantage of a very quiet, shy person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Really quiet' looks like one idea, very softly; it splits into SO and P.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is a feeble, timid person, one who would eat bread soaked in milk.

clue.text: Force workplace staff to accept extremely idiotic post

indicators.note: the two extremes of 'idiotic', I and C

parts.note: a staff is a pole or stick
the outer letters of idiotic
a post or station is a place of duty

explanation.surface: An employer forces staff to take on a pointless job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force workplace staff' reads as bullying employees, but 'Force workplace' is the definition: the police force works there.
explanation.definitionFit: A police station is where members of the police force are based.

clue.text: Range around East Timor's capital in train again

parts.note: a weapon's reach is its range

indicators.note: the capital letter of Timor

parts.note: E = East
the first letter of Timor

explanation.surface: A range of hills sits round the capital of East Timor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East Timor's capital' reads as Dili; it is only E plus Timor's first letter. ET goes in after the R of REACH.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the prefix re- means again and teaching is training, so the word is training a second time.

clue.text: Temp left firm over sign of indecision

parts.note: L = left

indicators.note: a thing knocked over lies the other way round

parts.note: CO = company, a firm
um is the hesitant noise of someone undecided

explanation.surface: A temporary worker walked out of a company, unable to make up their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'left' a verb, the temp quitting; it is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or clergyman standing in temporarily, a temp.

clue.text: Case of luxurious rings made of gold for distinguished people

indicators.note: the outside letters of luxurious, its case

parts.note: the outer letters of luxurious
aureate means golden, from Latin aurum

explanation.surface: A jewel case of plush golden rings made for the great and good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings' looks like jewellery sitting in the case; it is the verb, the case surrounding the gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Laureates are people honoured with a prize or title, such as Nobel laureates.

clue.text: Caught short, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to contract an illness is to catch it
a word like can't is a shortened form of cannot, so short in the grammatical sense

explanation.surface: Someone is caught needing a toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught short' is an idiom for suddenly needing the loo; split it, and each word defines the answer. 'Perhaps' flags that shortened is only one kind of contracted.
explanation.definitionFit: You contract (catch) an illness, and a contracted word is shortened, like 'can't'.

clue.text: Curiously wanting one less good qualification for mechanics

indicators.note: the letters are arranged oddly

parts.note: the letters of the words themselves
G = good, removed before the rearranging

explanation.surface: Oddly lacking a good qualification to be a mechanic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a car mechanic's certificate; the mechanics are Newton's laws of motion, and 'Newtonian' qualifies them as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Newtonian mechanics is classical physics, so the word qualifies 'mechanics'.

clue.text: Retiring female loves husband, maybe a bit of an ass

definitions.text: maybe a bit of an ass

indicators.note: going back, so FOOH is read in reverse

parts.note: F = female
love is O, a nil score in tennis; two of them
H = husband

explanation.surface: A shy woman adores her husband, though he is a bit of an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of an ass' sounds like a mild insult for the husband; it is literal, part of a donkey. 'Maybe' is there because many animals have hooves.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey stands on hooves, so a hoof is one part of an ass.

clue.text: Goods transporter about to board plane

parts.note: a fighter is a military plane
re = about, concerning

explanation.surface: Cargo is about to be loaded on to an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to board' reads as 'on the point of boarding'; 'about' is RE and 'to board' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a ship or aircraft that carries freight, goods.

clue.text: Court disaster, like pro donning sportswear

parts.note: as = like
kit is sports clothing
pro = for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A tennis court calamity, as a professional player dresses in the wrong gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' and 'pro' suggest tennis; 'court' is the verb, to invite, and 'pro' means in favour.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone who behaves recklessly is said to deserve the trouble that follows, just as one who courts disaster invites it.

clue.text: Sandwich, say? Wife tucked into large quantity

indicators.note: something tucked into another is pushed inside it

parts.note: a ton, or tons, is a lot
W = wife

explanation.surface: A wife tucks into a huge pile of sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich is not the snack but a town in Kent, south-east England; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandwich is a small historic town in Kent, one example of a town.

clue.text: Supposed snobs mixed with elite

indicators.note: the letters of both words are mixed together

parts.note: used as written
used as written

explanation.surface: So-called snobs rubbing shoulders with the real upper crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supposed' could be a verb; the answer needs the adjective, as in 'the supposed reason'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible means apparent or claimed, as a supposed reason may not be the real one.

clue.text: Entertainment shows gun users regularly ignored

parts.note: to gun an engine is to rev it

indicators.note: every other letter of users is dropped, keeping U, E, S

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of users

explanation.surface: Performances where people carrying guns are routinely overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gun users' looks like one idea, shooters; 'gun' is the verb for racing an engine, and 'users' is thinned out.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a light theatrical entertainment of sketches, songs and dances.

clue.text: Stand, carrying a single wide hamper

parts.note: a stall is a market stand
a single is one
W = wide, the cricket scoring abbreviation for a ball bowled out of the batter's reach

explanation.surface: A market stand is loaded with one broad picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' sits in the picture as a basket; it is the verb, to obstruct.
explanation.definitionFit: To stonewall is to obstruct by stalling or refusing to cooperate, so to hamper.

clue.text: Producer of fibre products is altering bags

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer inside it, as a bag holds things

parts.note: productS IS ALtering

explanation.surface: A company making fibre goods is changing its packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is altering' looks like an anagram signal for 'is'; the answer lies intact across the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is an agave plant whose leaves yield a tough fibre used for rope and twine.

clue.text: Cast is entertaining, pocketing 50 grand

indicators.note: to pocket is to put away inside

parts.note: an entertaining evening is fun
L is the Roman numeral 50
G = grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: An entertaining actor pockets a £50,000 fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the actors of a play; it is the past tense of throw. '50 grand' reads as one sum but splits into L and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Flung is the past tense of fling, and 'cast' can mean thrown.

clue.text: Time to leave religious headgear for Pope

parts.note: the turban is worn by Sikh men as a religious observance
T = time, removed

explanation.surface: It is time to swap religious headwear for the papal kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious headgear for Pope' calls up a mitre; the Pope is simply the answer, and eight popes were called Urban.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban is a papal name; Urban II launched the First Crusade.

clue.text: Spurs ground is lit, letting in header from Man United

indicators.note: IS LIT is ground up and rearranged
the rearranged letters let MU in
a header is what sits at the top, so this takes the first letter of Man

parts.note: the letters as written, before rearranging
the first letter of Man
U = United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: Tottenham's floodlit stadium hosts a Manchester United header.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spurs ground' is Tottenham Hotspur's stadium in football, but 'Spurs' is the definition and 'ground' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimuli are things that spur action, spurs in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Cheesy dish cooked just a little moment

parts.note: rare meat is only lightly cooked
'wait a bit' means wait a moment

explanation.surface: A cheese dish is flashed under the grill for only a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just a little moment' looks like one phrase; the split falls after 'little'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit, or Welsh rarebit, is melted cheese sauce on toast.

clue.text: Advance across shifting sand in coastal site

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it

indicators.note: SAND's letters shift to ANDS

parts.note: used as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Troops push forward over the dunes of a beach.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the rocky headland at the western tip of Cornwall, England's far south-west.
explanation.definitionFit: Land's End is a famous coastal headland and tourist site in Cornwall.

clue.text: Fan of grass cuckoo nest that's covered round river

indicators.note: crazy, so NEST is rearranged

parts.note: used as written, then rearranged
O is round in shape
R = river

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher fond of grassland finds a cuckoo's nest hidden by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan of grass' suggests a lawn lover; grass is slang for cannabis. 'Cuckoo' is not the bird but the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoner is a habitual cannabis user, a fan of grass in the slang sense.
